name: parr-flash-council-office
prompt: Portrait-format documentary photograph, midday, inside the reception of a tired modern British district council office. Magnolia walls scuffed at hip height, a long laminate counter in fake beech with a peeling edge strip, a red take-a-number dispenser on a chrome pole with a paper tongue sticking out, a perspex leaflet rack of sun-faded flyers on recycling and council tax, a row of bolted orange plastic chairs, a sad yucca in a pot, carpet tiles in municipal grey. Five figures queue in a tidy line in front of the counter, shoulders slumped like people who have been here an hour, every head tipped back to stare upward. Behind the counter, crammed wall to wall, rises an enormous heap of printed paper, dog-eared and bulging, which bursts through the suspended ceiling where one square tile has been knocked loose and dangles from the grid; taped to the heap at eye level is one laminated A4 sheet printed in plain black capitals: THE RULES. Each of the five wears a knitted balaclava in a loud colour that clashes with the next: lime green, bubblegum pink, traffic-cone orange, cobalt blue, egg-yolk yellow. Their faces are smooth solid knit from brow to chin, featureless cloth where eyes, nose and mouth would be. A thick white stitched circle frames the whole front of each head, and high inside it, on the wearer's left side so it lands on the viewer's right near two o'clock, a red triangle with softened corners is sewn on, never centred. Below the hoods: a shiny polyester tracksuit, a cheap rain anorak, a puffer jacket, collars zipped up over the neck, sleeves pulled past the wrists, cotton gloves on both hands of every figure, not a scrap of skin anywhere. The figure at the front of the queue holds a small numbered ticket between gloved fingers. Shot straight on at chest height with a wide-angle lens from a few steps back, deep focus, the frame stuffed with clutter to every edge. Lit by one hard flash fired from the camera into daylight, so the colours of the knitwear and plastic come out saturated and slightly garish, a glossy glare bounces off the counter, crisp dark cast-shadows sit on the wall behind each figure, and the room's corners fall off a touch darker. Palette and texture of slow colour-negative film from a high-street minilab: over-bright, a little cheap, fine grain. Deadpan, unstaged, quietly absurd.
